sections.title: How the repertoire fits together
paras: This repertoire is built on 1.e4. It chooses set-ups that are easy to understand and share ideas: the Italian structure with c3 and d3 against 1...e5, the 2.c3 system against 1...c5, and the Advance set-up against 1...e6 and 1...c6.
The common thread is a strong centre. White aims for pawns on d4 and e4 (or e5), develops naturally and castles, then chooses a plan based on the pawn structure.
Use the explorer to read each line with its notes, then switch to Drill mode, where the trainer plays Black’s replies and you play White’s moves. Lines you get wrong come back in your review queue.
sections.key: Read each line in the explorer, then drill it until you can play your side without help.

sections.title: Against 1...e5
paras: Against 1...e5, White plays 2.Nf3 and, after 2...Nc6, the Italian set-up with Bc4, c3 and d3. The pawns stay flexible and White builds slowly, keeping d3-d4 in reserve. Against Black’s other second moves White takes the centre with d2-d4.

sections.title: Against 1...c5
paras: Against 1...c5, White plays 2.c3, preparing d2-d4 so that White can recapture with a pawn and keep a full centre. The positions are clear and don’t require memorizing long forcing lines.

sections.title: Typical middlegame plans
paras: The knight route d2-f1-g3. In the Italian structure the queen’s knight has no good square on c3, where it would block the c-pawn. It travels d2, f1 and g3 (or e3) instead, where it eyes f5 and supports d3-d4.

Playing with an isolated pawn. Several lines against 1...c5 give White an isolated d-pawn. In return White gets open lines and active pieces. Keep pieces on the board, use the e5 square for a knight, and look for the d4-d5 break.

Advance structures. With pawns on d4 and e5, White has space on the kingside. Keep the d4-pawn well protected, since it is the base of the chain, and answer ...c4 by playing on the kingside or with b2-b3 to open lines.

Classical set-ups against fianchettos. Against ...g6 and ...Bg7, White keeps the centre with pawns on d4 and e4, develops with Nc3, Nf3 and Be2, and castles. The plan is to keep the centre secure so that Black’s bishop bites on granite.
sections.key: Every line has a plan: know which structure you are aiming for.

sections.title: Drill: every line
paras: The trainer plays your opponent’s moves, choosing among the branches of the repertoire, and you play your side. When you leave the repertoire, the trainer shows the move and its explanation, and the line goes into your review queue.
sections.key: Play your side from memory; read the note whenever a move surprises you.
